observations:
LM2 Torah 114 is a three-sentence personal testimony — not a structured conceptual teaching. The complete text records R' Nathan walking with Rebbe Nachman in silence, until the Rebbe uttered a single Yiddish sentence: 'Es hot a panim az me muz zikh fun a hirur zeyer hitn' (it seems that one must guard oneself very much from a hirur). Nathan adds that he then understood from the Rebbe's holy tone and movements that at that moment the Rebbe was shown in his awesome attainments the enormity of the damage of hirur (פְּגַם הַהִרְהוּר), which harms exceedingly. The text ends: 'And it is impossible to describe this in writing.'

The teaching contains no bechina language ('X הוא בחינת Y', 'X נקרא Y', 'X כנ"ל'). The word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear. The only concepts named are הִרְהוּר (the improper thought itself) and פְּגַם הַהִרְהוּר (its damage), and their relationship is causal — the hirur produces the damage — which is eitza, not bechina. They are not two expressions of the same essential nature; one is the cause and the other is the effect.

A new package requires three or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. That condition is entirely unmet here. There are no candidate nodes, no equating language, and no ontological topology to map. The text is, by its own admission, a testimony to something that cannot be put into words.

Conclusion: NO_NEW_PACKAGES. The dataset correctly has zero entries for reference 1114, and there is nothing in the source text that warrants adding any bechina edges or constructing any packages.
